title: Differential fibre finrank comparison above a prime
statement: Let k be a field, S a finite type k-algebra, q a prime of S, and let K be algebraically closed over k with a maximal prime qK of K tensor_k S contracting to q. Then the finrank of the Kähler differential fibre at qK equals that at q.

source.place: Tag 00TT, proof of (2) => (1), construction of K and m; Tag 00RV for differential base change. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00TT.

proof.text: Install the tensor product right S-algebra structure. Contraction gives the S-algebra residue-field embedding f : kappa(q) to kappa(qK), using Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ. Its algebra structure gives IsScalarTower S kappa(q) kappa(qK).

Base-change the inverse of KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquiv k K S B to L = kappa(qK), and use TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange S B L L to obtain the L-linear equivalence from the differential fibre over B to L tensor_S Omega[S/k].

Compose with the inverse of cancelBaseChange S kappa(q) L L to identify this with L tensor_kappa(q) (kappa(q) tensor_S Omega[S/k]). Apply e.finrank_eq and Module.finrank_baseChange. No flatness or smoothness is needed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00TT (explicit geometric point construction) and Tag 00RV (differential base change); read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00TT and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00RV on 2026-10-13.

theorem algClosed_prime_over_finrank_differentials_eq
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [FiniteType k S]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum S)
    (K : Type (max u v)) (_hK : Field K) (_hAk : Algebra k K) (_hCK : IsAlgClosed K)
    (qK : PrimeSpectrum (K ⊗[k] S))
    (_hmax : qK.asIdeal.IsMaximal)
    (hq : PrimeSpectrum.comap
      (TensorProduct.includeRight : S →ₐ[k] K ⊗[k] S).toRingHom qK = q) :
    Module.finrank qK.asIdeal.ResidueField
        (qK.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[K ⊗[k] S] KaehlerDifferential K (K ⊗[k] S)) =
      Module.finrank q.asIdeal.ResidueField
        (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] KaehlerDifferential k S)
